The Last of Us was released in the Summer of 2013. It is an action-adventure survival horror game developed by Naughty Dog as a PS3 exclusive and was later re-released on the PS4 with a myriad of upgrades to the graphics, frame rate, and controls. At the games initial release, it saw an abundance of praise from the games press, receiving over 100 awards within its first year and some 10/10 scores from IGN and Destructoid. So The Last of Us must be one of the greatest games to have ever blessed the Earth right? Well in my opinion, no.

This is a single player mode review without playing the DLC.

The Good:

  • Some of the best character development I've seen in a video game ever between the two main characters
  • The game environments are colorful, true to life, and tell stories all on their own
  • The recently post-apocalyptic atmosphere is nailed as there are still military checkpoints, deadly spore filled houses, raider settlements and more
  • Camera angles during cinematic cut-scenes are smooth and play greatly into what is happening on screen
  • Story pacing is fantastic and leads the player to wanting to play more to find out what happens next
  • Playing as Ellie changes up gameplay, adds a new mechanic, and leaves you vulnerable in a good way
  • Charming dialogue from Ellie and some of the supporting cast make for some great moments
  • The controls work fine and are a familiar configuration

The Bad:

  • The gameplay pacing feels like it didn't hit the mark
  • Easily manipulated brain-dead enemy AI
  • Crouch walking encouraged at almost all times during gameplay leads to very slow movement and brings the game to a snails pace
  • Lack of variety in enemy types and encounters
  • Weapon balancing and ammo/loot pickups feel like an afterthought
  • Melee combat is hit or miss and feels like a lazily implemented system
  • While the story is the best part of The Last of Us, by the end of it, I felt like I was only told a small part of a much bigger story
  • The supporting character development feels a bit lacking in Tess, Sarah, and Tommy

Criticisms

I'll now get into a more detailed criticism about what I mentioned above and include a few other things that I took note of. The first hour of the game is a very slow paced tutorial that you're forced to suffer through even in New Game +. Your ability to sprint, craft, climb, ect. is all slowly taught to you without any ability to speed things up. Even before the tutorial, the game has you play a small backstory section that may mislead players into thinking the game is more of a walking simulator with QTE's instead of a gameplay heavy survival horror game. While the game is mostly about the gameplay after these portions, it doesn't get much better from here in the gameplay aspect.

 

The object of the game goes from taking Ellie to the Fireflies home base, to not getting caught in any enemy encounters. The Last of Us instantly becomes exclusively a stealth experience as soon as you leave the tutorial section. Sneaking via crouch walking is the best way to get around undetected. The best way to kill enemies is to stealthily take them down with a shiv, a one hit kill. With the abundance of crafting materials left around and lack of ammo I think you may see where this is going. The combination of the blind, brain-dead AI, encouraged crouch walk, one hit kill shivs in abundance, why would anyone play any differently? The shivs get upgrades as well, mine could hold 3 charges, meaning I could kill 3 people with 1 shiv and you are capable of holding up to 3. 9 kills with the shivs you have on hand and 9 more from the maxed out crafting materials you'll inevitably find and you have 18 instant kills on hand. You may think that seems unbalanced but surely there are enemies you can't stab right? Well you'd be correct, there is one enemy that can't be stabbed. Of the what seems like 4 enemy types, only the Bloaters can't be stabbed.

 

This leads me into the enemy variety and encounters. There are actually what seems like 3 different human type enemies and 4 different infected enemies. You have your regular human enemy, your heavy human enemy who wears armor and usually has a shotgun or assault rifle, and a grenadier that throws molotov cocktails at you. The distinction between these character types end up not mattering much in practice as you just sneak behind them and stab them if given the chance anyways. Then there are the infected enemies: Runners, Stalkers, Clickers, and Bloaters. There is a distinct difference between runners, clickers, and bloaters. I could never tell the difference between runners and stalkers as they are so similar, and only read about their existence in game and online. Clickers are an interesting enemy as they can 1 hit kill you if you don't have a shiv to use as a defense. They're blind though, so nothing stops you from slowly crouch walking up to their face and stabbing them with a shiv, eliminating their effectiveness. Bloaters are a boss type character that I only encountered 3 or 4 times and only had to fight 1 or 2 of them, 1 being mandatory. This leads into the encounter variety. Far too often you are in a building or some tunnels and you have to sneak around a room filled with 2-4 enemies. There were only 2 instances in the game where I felt Ellie and Joel were in any danger because of the sheer amount of enemies. This is really disappointing as there could have been some great memorable scenes filled with both humans and infected fighting each other that you could have navigated through. This is never explored however, as you are either in an area of the game with infected or humans, not both simultaneously.

 

The gameplay takes a back seat to the story, but your time spent in game is almost exclusively controlled by the player. I feel that the gameplay being as mediocre as it is could pass, if there were more cutscenes and QTE's. I personally don't like this model of game however and would prefer that the gameplay would have been worked on in more detail. The crafting system, while interesting, seems very limited and left me wanting some more complexity. Same goes for the melee system. It is just a mash fest that Joel almost always wins. I mentioned weapon balancing a bit with the shivs, but for the actual weapons, not all guns are useful. That would perfectly fine, except when you add in a weapon upgrade system. While upgrading my bow, I could see and feel where my upgrades were going. The revolver however doesn't feel much better from where it started. There just seems to be a lot of interesting gameplay mechanics that weren't fully fleshed out and instead left in a mediocre state.

Conclusion

I really enjoyed playing The Last of Us even if I have a lot of criticisms about it. The story is interesting and seems well thought out. I'm excited to see it flourish in the next few games that will inevitably be released by Naughty Dog. This is a game that has the potential to be great (as we saw with some of the gameplay mechanics showed off at e3 before its release) but just misses the mark. I hope some of the gameplay problems can be addressed in future iterations, but with all the praise it received, I'm not so sure that'll happen (if it ain't broke, don't fix it). With limited replayability I'd say its worth buying used or renting from a friend. Gameplay-wise I'd give it a rating of 5 or 6, story-wise i'd give it an 8.5 or 9. All together though, I'd give the game a 7.5/10.

This is a single player mode review without playing the DLC.
